key_insight: Among 58,007 ClinicalTrials.gov trials, 99.44% reported sex but only 0.95% reported gender, revealing a major reporting gap.
clinical_relevance: More complete sex and gender reporting could help researchers assess whose experiences trial evidence represents.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of interventional trials with results posted from January 2009 through April 2026.
Examined trial characteristics associated with sex and gender reporting.
Compared female participation with disease burden using participation-to-prevalence ratios (PPRs) across 10 conditions.
evidence_signal: Across 15,552 mixed-sex trials covering 10 conditions, median PPR ranged from 0.68 for COPD to 1.05 for obesity; female participation was relatively lower in 8 conditions.
watch_item: Registry reporting and observational associations cannot establish why representation gaps occur or capture unreported participant identities.
paper_title: Sex and Gender Reporting and Female Participation Relative to Disease Burden in ClinicalTrials.gov
